title: Get a dog license
question: Does my dog need a county license, and how do I get one?
office: Department of Finance & Budget (dog licensing administered by the contractor PetData)
summary: Every dog 4 months or older owned by an Albemarle County resident needs a county license. Get it within 30 days of the dog turning 4 months, getting the dog, or moving into the county. Licenses expire December 31; renew by January 31. The County's contractor PetData sells them online ($2.00 convenience fee per transaction) or by mail with a check or money order payable to County of Albemarle. The dog must be currently vaccinated against rabies (or have a health department exemption). A one-year license costs $5 for a spayed or neutered dog and $10 for an unaltered dog; two- and three-year licenses are sold if the rabies vaccination lasts. Kennels pay $50 per ten dogs. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs pay no tax.

steps.step: Check whether your dog needs an Albemarle County license
steps.who: The owner or custodian of the dog, if they live in Albemarle County
steps.how: Every dog 4 months old or older owned by a county resident must be licensed and wear the tag. A releasing agency (a shelter or rescue) registered with the County is exempt. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs still get a license but pay no license tax (see s4). Emotional support animals are not service dogs under state law. What counts is where you live, not a Charlottesville mailing address: if you live inside the City of Charlottesville, license the dog with the City Treasurer instead, because the County can license only dogs of county residents.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old, after you get a dog 4 months or older, or after you move into the county with one (PetData; Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A); County Code § 4-201(A))

steps.step: Have the dog vaccinated against rabies and keep the certificate
steps.who: Owner; a licensed veterinarian (or a licensed veterinary technician under the veterinarian's direct supervision)
steps.how: The veterinarian gives you a rabies vaccination certificate. By law the veterinarian also sends a copy, or its details, within 45 days to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination is given (for a vaccination in Albemarle, the County's Director of Finance), and certificates for dogs that live elsewhere are passed on to the owner's locality. The County matches these reports against its license records. Check that the certificate shows your correct address and your dog's details. If you want a two- or three-year license, the vaccination must stay valid for the whole license term.
steps.deadline: The dog must be currently vaccinated from 4 months of age (Va. Code § 3.2-6521(A))
steps.quote: The supervising veterinarian on the premises shall provide the owner or custodian of the dog or the cat with a rabies vaccination certificate or herd rabies vaccination certificate and shall keep a copy in his own files.

steps.step: Only if the dog cannot safely be vaccinated: get a rabies vaccination exemption certificate
steps.who: Your veterinarian applies; the local health director (Virginia Department of Health, Blue Ridge Health District, Charlottesville/Albemarle Health Department), in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, decides
steps.how: The health director may grant an exemption only if vaccination would likely endanger the dog's life because of a previously diagnosed disease or other medical condition documented by a licensed veterinarian. The veterinarian consults the local health department and submits the Department of Health exemption request form with the supporting medical records (the health department may ask for more). If it is approved, the health department issues an exemption certificate to the veterinarian, to you and to the local animal control office. Send that certificate to PetData in place of a vaccination certificate.
steps.deadline: The exemption is valid for one year; then the dog must be vaccinated or the exemption renewed (12VAC5-105-30(B))
steps.quote: Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination may be presented in lieu of a rabies vaccination certificate for the purposes of veterinary inspection by designated local authorities and for the purposes of licensing by the locality where the animal resides.

steps.step: Choose the license term and work out the fee
steps.how: Licenses run for one, two or three years and all expire on December 31. You can buy a two-year license if the rabies vaccination expires two years from the current year, or a three-year license if it expires three or more years from the current year; a one-year license needs a vaccination that is current on the day you buy. The tax is $5 a year for a spayed or neutered dog and $10 a year for an unaltered dog. Paying the spayed or neutered rate certifies that the dog is spayed or neutered. A trained guide, hearing or service dog pays no license tax; the form has no box for it, so ask PetData customer service how to claim the exemption. PetData gives no refund for unused license time, or if you paid the unaltered rate and the dog is spayed or neutered later in the term. A dog that turns 4 months or arrives between November 1 and December 31 pays for the next calendar year, licensed from the date you pay.
steps.fee: Spayed/neutered dog: $5.00 (1 year), $10.00 (2 years), $15.00 (3 years). Unaltered dog: $10.00, $20.00, $30.00. No tax for a trained guide, hearing or service dog.
steps.quote: Multi-year licenses are available based on the remaining term of the dog’s current rabies vaccination.

steps.step: Apply and pay online through PetData
steps.how: Start from PetData's Albemarle County License Online page and follow the link to its online licensing system. Several pets can go in one transaction. Pay by credit card (the page shows Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover). Scan and upload the rabies certificate, or send it later by fax, mail or email; the license is issued only once all required documents arrive. Kennel licenses (and dangerous dog registrations) cannot be bought online: use the mail option.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the dog turns 4 months, is acquired or comes to the county; renewals by January 31 (PetData; County Code § 4-201(A))
steps.fee: The license tax (see s4) plus a $2.00 convenience fee per online transaction
steps.quote: If you would like to register online, a convenience fee of $2.00 will apply for each transaction.

steps.step: Or apply by mail to Albemarle County Dog Licensing, c/o PetData
steps.how: Enclose a copy of the dog's current rabies certificate (or exemption certificate) and, if you like, the completed Albemarle County Dog License Application (optional). Pay by check or money order payable to "County of Albemarle"; do not send cash. Mail it to Albemarle County Dog Licensing, c/o PetData, PO Box 141929, Irving, TX 75014-1929. Paperwork is not returned, so keep copies. A payment the bank returns unpaid for insufficient funds carries a $35.00 administrative fee.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the dog turns 4 months, is acquired or comes to the county; renewals by January 31 (PetData; County Code § 4-201(A))
steps.fee: The license tax (see s4); $35.00 administrative fee if the payment is returned unpaid for insufficient funds
steps.quote: The license application below may be downloaded and included, but it is not required.

steps.step: PetData checks the application and mails the license receipt and metal tag
steps.who: PetData, for the Department of Finance & Budget (the Director of Finance is the licensing officer under the County Code)
steps.how: The County licenses only dogs of county residents and may ask for information showing you live in the county. With a complete application, payment and a current rabies certificate, PetData mails the license receipt and metal tag. If a document or the right payment is missing, PetData sends an Incomplete License Letter asking for the missing items (or returns everything), and processing is delayed. Return the letter with what it asks for; a wrong-amount check must be replaced, not altered. License application information is kept and open to public inspection while the license is valid.
steps.deadline: PetData mails the tag and receipt within 10 business days after it receives the completed application and payment; allow 3 to 5 more business days for delivery
steps.quote: We will mail your tag and license receipt within 10 business days from the day we receive your completed license application and payment.

steps.step: Put the tag on the dog's collar and keep the receipt
steps.how: Fasten the tag to a sturdy collar that the dog wears at all times. Keep the license receipt and show it if an animal control officer or other officer asks. The collar and tag may come off while the dog is lawfully hunting, competing in a dog show, confined, under your immediate control, or has a skin condition a collar would worsen. A dog without a tag is presumed unlicensed, and a dog running at large without one is taken to the public animal shelter (the Charlottesville-Albemarle SPCA).
steps.quote: Any dog owner shall securely fasten dog license tags to a substantial collar and ensure that the collar and license tag are worn by the dog.

steps.step: Renew before the license runs out
steps.who: Owner; PetData sends the renewal notices
steps.how: PetData mails a renewal notice before the license expires; it shows the rabies expiration date on file. If the rabies vaccination is also expiring, have the dog re-vaccinated and send the new certificate with the renewal payment. Renew online or by mail as in s5 or s6. If you do not respond, PetData sends a past-due notice about 60 days after the first and then a final (orange postcard) notice, each asking you to license within 10 days. If the dog has died, you no longer have it, or you moved out of the county, tell PetData instead of paying.
steps.deadline: Licenses expire on December 31 and must be renewed by January 31; the County Code makes it a violation not to pay before February 1
steps.quote: Licenses expire on December 31st, and must be renewed by January 31st.

steps.step: If a vaccinated dog is not licensed, expect a billing notice
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, through PetData
steps.how: The County matches the rabies vaccination reports from veterinarians against its license records. If a vaccinated dog has not been licensed within 90 days of the vaccination, the County (through PetData) sends the owner an application or billing notice asking for a completed application and the license tax. Pay as in s5 or s6, or tell PetData if the dog has died, was rehomed, or you live outside the county.
steps.deadline: Sent when no license has been applied for within 90 days after the vaccination (County Code § 4-205; Va. Code § 3.2-6529(B))

steps.step: Keep your details current; a license cannot be transferred
steps.how: Use PetData's update pages to report a new address, phone or email, a move out of the county, a corrected pet description or rabies vaccination, or that you no longer own the dog or it has died. A license belongs to one owner and one dog: a new owner, or a different dog, needs a new license.
steps.quote: Licenses may not be transferred from one owner to another owner or from one pet to another pet.

steps.step: Replace a lost, destroyed or stolen tag
steps.who: Owner or custodian; PetData for the Director of Finance
steps.how: Mail a $1.00 check or money order payable to "County of Albemarle" (no cash) to Albemarle County Dog Licensing, c/o PetData, PO Box 141929, Irving, TX 75014-1929, with a copy of your earlier license receipt or a note saying which pet the tag is for. Only one tag can be active per dog. The County Code and state law also speak of presenting the original receipt and an affidavit that the tag was lost, destroyed or stolen; PetData's instructions do not ask for an affidavit. Put the new tag on the collar right away.
steps.deadline: Immediately, as the County Code states (County Code § 4-203; Va. Code § 3.2-6532 says at once)
steps.quote: You may include either a copy of your prior license receipt or a note to designate the pet for which you are purchasing a replacement tag.

steps.step: Kennels: buy an annual kennel license by mail
steps.who: Kennel owner (an establishment keeping five or more dogs for breeding, hunting, training, renting, buying, boarding, selling or showing); PetData
steps.how: The County Code sets a kennel license tax (state law lets a county do so); neither the County Code nor PetData says whether a kennel must use it instead of licensing each dog (see caveats). A kennel license covers a block of up to ten dogs, at $50.00 per block, and cannot be bought online. Apply by mail to PetData as in s6, ticking the kennel license box on the application. Fasten the kennel tag to the kennel enclosure in full view and keep one of the identification plates that come with it on the collar of each dog in the kennel; keep unused plates and show them if an officer asks.
steps.deadline: Due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(C))
steps.fee: $50.00 per block of ten dogs (County Code § 4-204(C)); PetData lists $50.00 for a kennel of up to 10 dogs
steps.quote: The kennel owner shall securely fasten the license tag to the kennel enclosure in full view and keep one of the identification plates provided with the license tag attached to the collar of each dog authorized to be kept enclosed in the kennel.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The How Do I page (https://www.albemarle.org/how-do-i/licensing/dog-licensing) redirects to the Dog Licenses page. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act.

PetData (petdata.com) is a private contractor, not a County office. Its pages and the application PDF state the County's fees and rules, but where they differ from the County Code (below), the Code governs. No terms of use were found on the PetData site. The online licensing system itself (https://secure.petdata.com/petlicense/muni/abm/) is a payment flow and is not described here.

Local law source. Municode, which publishes the current Albemarle County Code (PetData links § 4-200 there: https://library.municode.com/va/albemarle_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=CH4AN_ART2DO_DIV1LI_S4-200DOLITAREBEPADOLIREBEOBEX), forbids automated access under its terms, so the current Code text has not been checked. County Code quotes come from 'A - Proposed Ordinance' attached to Board of Supervisors Legistar matter 18-508 (Ordinance No. 18-4(1), rewriting Chapter 4), from the county's Legistar records (webapi.legistar.com). The matter history records it as 'ADOPTED ordinance.' on October 3, 2018. The attachment is the draft: its clerk's certification is blank. Struck (deleted) and hidden text in the draft is left out; Division 1 (§§ 4-200 to 4-209) carries no strike-through. Legistar titles from 2019 to 2026 show Chapter 4 amendments to definitions (§ 4-103), dangerous and vicious dogs (§§ 4-210 to 4-222), dogs running at large and leash rules, and animal noise (§ 4-319), but none to the license division, and a search of titles containing 'Animal', 'Dog', 'Chapter 4' and 'License' (2026-10-11) found no matter amending §§ 4-200 to 4-209 after 2018. The current Municode section name for § 4-200 matches the 2018 heading, but the current text has not been compared. Legistar's record of the October 3, 2018 meeting item (event 1147) says only 'ADOPTED ordinance.' and has an empty minutes note, so whether the Board changed the draft at adoption is not recorded there. The fees and procedure in the 2018 text match PetData's current pages.

Errors in the 2018 text. County Code § 4-206 cites 'Virginia Code § 16.2-69.48:1'; the state section is § 16.1-69.48:1 (as § 3.2-6536 reads). The § 4-204 heading reads 'Amount of license dog tax.' Neither is quoted as law here.

When a license is first needed. The County's Dog Licenses page says a license is needed 'after their first rabies shot', while state law (§ 3.2-6524(A)) and County Code § 4-200 tie it to the dog being 4 months old, and the application says 'over 4 months old'. Rabies vaccination is itself required from 4 months (§ 3.2-6521(A)), so the dates normally coincide. The 4-month rule is the legal one.

Newcomers. PetData says to license within 30 days of moving into the county. State law (§ 3.2-6530(A)) speaks only of reaching 4 months or acquiring a dog. County Code § 4-201(A)(1) and (2) speak of a dog over 4 months, unlicensed by the County, coming into the possession of a County resident. No source says whether a license from another locality counts for any time after a move; the County Code licenses only county residents (§ 4-202(B)).

Due dates. PetData says payment is due January 31 and licenses expire December 31. County Code § 4-201(A) says the tax is due no later than January 31 of each license year, and § 4-201(B) makes non-payment before February 1 a violation. A dog that turns 4 months or arrives between November 1 and December 31 pays for the following calendar year (§ 4-201(A)(2)). PetData's past-due and final notices ask owners to license 'within 10 days'. That is PetData's request, not a legal deadline.

Replacement tags. County Code § 4-203(A) and Va. Code § 3.2-6532 call for the original license receipt and an affidavit that the tag was lost, destroyed or stolen. PetData's FAQ asks only for a copy of the prior receipt or a note naming the pet. Follow PetData's instructions, but be ready to give a sworn statement if asked.

Service dogs. Neither the application nor PetData's pages mention the guide, hearing and service dog exemption, or how to claim it. Ask PetData customer service. The exemption covers trained dogs as defined in Va. Code § 51.5-40.1; emotional support, comfort or companionship animals do not qualify.

No lifetime license. Albemarle offers 1-, 2- and 3-year licenses only. State law lets a locality offer a lifetime license (§ 3.2-6530(B)), but the 2018 County Code provides none. The multi-year fees ($10 or $15 for a spayed or neutered dog, $20 or $30 for an unaltered dog) equal $5 or $10 a year, within the state cap.

Where to apply. The County's page and PetData list only online and mail licensing. Neither says whether the Finance & Budget office at 401 McIntire Road sells licenses in person. PetData's pages mention sending documents by fax or email, but no fax number or email address appears on the Albemarle pages read; email goes through PetData's web form. Payment methods: credit card online (Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover are shown); check or money order by mail. PetData's Payment Options page (https://petdata.com/for-pet-owners/abm/payment) also lists only these two: by mail with a check or money order payable to 'County of Albemarle', or online with a major credit card. PetData's corporate Contact Us page lists a company fax number and general mailbox, but no page says they are the channels for Albemarle license documents, so they are not recorded as contacts.

Returned payment fee. The $35.00 fee is stated by PetData and on the application. No County ordinance setting it was read. Va. Code § 15.2-106 lets a locality set, by ordinance, a fee of up to $50 for a returned payment.

Releasing agencies. State law exempts a releasing agency 'that has registered as such annually with local animal control'. The 2018 County Code says 'registered with the County'. How a shelter or rescue registers in Albemarle is not covered here.

Penalties. Owning an unlicensed dog, not paying the tax before February 1, making a false statement to get a license, and harboring an unlicensed dog are Class 4 misdemeanors (Va. Code §§ 3.2-6524(A) and 3.2-6587(A)(1), (2), (7) and (9); County Code §§ 4-104, 4-201(B), 4-202(F), 4-209; the County page says 'Failure to comply with the license requirement is a Class 4 misdemeanor.'). The fine is not more than $250 (§ 18.2-11(d)). The court may also order the dog confiscated (§ 3.2-6587(A)(2)), and paying after a summons does not avoid court costs (§ 3.2-6536; County Code § 4-206).

No administrative appeal. No statute or County source gives an administrative appeal from a refusal to issue a dog license. Refusals turn on the rabies certificate and residence. The routes listed in escalation are practical: cure the defect, ask PetData, then the Department of Finance & Budget, which contracts with PetData. That 'internal appeal' rung is not a formal appeal. Refund statutes for erroneously assessed local taxes (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3980 to 58.1-3990) were not established to reach the Title 3.2 dog license tax, so they are not listed. The PetData-County contract was not read.

Who licenses. Albemarle has no elected treasurer. The Director of Finance holds the treasurer's powers (Va. Code § 15.2-522) and is named as the licensing officer in County Code §§ 4-202 to 4-205. PetData acts as the County's agent (§ 3.2-6527 lets the treasurer appoint agents). PetData's FAQ says the County privatized licensing beginning in 2019.

Veterinarian reports. The County page says veterinarians report to the treasurer of the locality where the veterinarian practices. Va. Code § 3.2-6529(A) says the locality where the vaccination occurs. County Code § 4-313(A) says to the County's Director of Finance. The Director must forward certificates for dogs of other localities' residents (§ 4-313(B)).

Shelter and Animal Control. Strays go to the Charlottesville-Albemarle SPCA, the County's contracted public animal shelter (County Code § 4-103 definition; PetData FAQ). Legistar matter 25-182 (2025) is titled 'Resolution Approving an Agreement with the Charlottesville-Albemarle Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals for Public Shelter Services.' The Legistar Web API lists it with status 'Agenda Ready' and no passed date. The agreement itself, and the SPCA's reclaim fees and hours, are not covered here. The number (434) 977-9041 is published by the County as the Animal Control officer's number. The City of Charlottesville's Animal Control page (https://www.charlottesville.gov/207/Animal-Control, as of 2026-10-11) gives the same number for non-emergency animal control calls through the Emergency Communications Center (ECC), so it is probably a shared dispatch line, not a direct office line. For emergencies, call 911. Animal Control is part of the Albemarle County Police Department; its own page is not covered here. A reclaiming owner may be charged the actual cost of impoundment (§ 3.2-6546(C)), and a locality may also set impoundment fees by ordinance after a public hearing; no Albemarle impoundment fee ordinance is covered here.

County Code § 4-227 (2018 text) has the same five-day hold and impoundment rules as Va. Code § 3.2-6546(C). Chapter 4's running-at-large sections were amended in 2019 and 2020, so only the state statute is used for the hold period.

Rabies clinics. The County must make sure a rabies clinic serves it at least once every two years (Va. Code § 3.2-6521(B); County Code § 4-312(E)). No current clinic schedule was found. Vaccination costs are set by veterinarians and are not stated by any County source.

Kennel license. Va. Code § 3.2-6528(A) lets an ordinance provide an annual license tax for kennels of 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 dogs, and the 2018 County Code § 4-204(C) sets $50.00 per block of ten dogs; PetData lists $50.00 for a kennel of up to 10 dogs. Neither the County Code nor PetData says whether an establishment that meets the kennel definition must buy a kennel license instead of licensing each dog, or how a kennel of more than ten dogs is billed on PetData's form. Ask PetData customer service.

Not covered. Dangerous dog registration ($150.00 initial, $85.00 renewal by January 31) is a separate process . It is on the same application but cannot be done online. No Albemarle cat license was found: the 2018 Code's license division covers dogs only, and cat licensing is optional for localities (§ 3.2-6524(B)). Residents of the Town of Scottsville live in the county and license with the County. No separate town rule is covered here.

Public records and privacy. Dog license application information is open to public inspection while the license is valid (Va. Code § 3.2-6527; County Code § 4-202(E)), and PetData offers a tag-number search for finders of lost pets. The 2018 ordinance's certification block and the court pages name officials and judges. No personal names are recorded here; only office channels are. The Health Department mailbox recorded is the office's environmental health address.

State law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, not to the law.lis.virginia.gov pages linked in each citation. Regulation quotes come from the Virginia Administrative Code page for 12VAC5-105-30 on law.lis.virginia.gov. The VDH exemption form (ris.dls.virginia.gov) has no fillable fields.

corrections: All 93 original quotes confirmed word for word: 41 state-law quotes against I.text_of for the cited section (subsection placement checked by reading the text), 5 regulation quotes against the law.lis.virginia.gov page for 12VAC5-105-30, 31 County Code quotes against a fresh copy of the Legistar attachment with struck and hidden runs blanked out (so no quote can span deleted text), 14 PetData quotes against the live pages and 2 County-page quotes against the Internet Archive copy of 2026-08-14 (still the newest capture). None needed removing.

Penalties: owning an unlicensed dog (Va. Code § 3.2-6524(A)) is a Class 4 misdemeanor under § 3.2-6587(A)(9), the catch-all that County Code § 4-104 cites, not under (A)(1), (2) or (7); added a legal_basis quote for (A)(9) and corrected the penalties caveat.

s2: state law sends the veterinarian's rabies report to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination is given, who passes on certificates for dogs living elsewhere (§ 3.2-6529; County Code § 4-313); the step had said the report always goes to the County's Director of Finance.

s3: added the regulation's condition for an exemption (vaccination would likely endanger the animal's life because of a previously diagnosed disease or documented medical condition) and that the health department may ask for more records (12VAC5-105-30(A), (B)).

Escalation rung for an impounded dog: added that the owner may be charged the actual cost of impoundment and that a dog not claimed by the end of the hold period is deemed abandoned and becomes the shelter's property (§ 3.2-6546(C), (D)); two legal_basis quotes and one fee entry added.

s4: the service-dog exemption is now 'ask PetData customer service how to claim it' (no source says to tell PetData on the application); added PetData's no-refund rule for unused time and later spaying or neutering, from its FAQ.
s13: the step no longer implies a kennel must buy a kennel license; neither the County Code nor PetData says so. Added a kennel-license caveat.
s1: reworded the City of Charlottesville point: residence, not a Charlottesville mailing address, decides which locality licenses the dog.
Summary: 'You need a current rabies certificate' now reads that the dog must be currently vaccinated or have a health department exemption, matching County Code § 4-202(A) and 12VAC5-105-30(B).

Caveats: petdata.com has no robots.txt (HTTP 404), not one that allows all; recorded PetData's Payment Options page (mail or online only); recorded the verifier's Legistar title search, the October 3, 2018 meeting item, matter 25-182's status, the City Animal Control page re-read, and the verifier's judgement on the Legistar Web API.

Contacts: the SPCA row now says the address comes from PetData's FAQ and the phone from the County page; the Animal Control row says the number is the non-emergency Emergency Communications Center line, with 911 for emergencies.

open_issues: www.albemarle.org still returns HTTP 403 to this client, robots.txt included (2026-10-11). The two County-page quotes and the Finance office contact were confirmed against Internet Archive copies of 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-16, which the archive index shows are the newest captures. Re-check the live pages.

The current County Code text (Municode) was not read because of that site's terms. The County Code quotes come from the 2018 draft attached to Legistar matter 18-508, which the Legistar record shows as adopted on October 3, 2018 with no note of changes at adoption; no later matter amends §§ 4-200 to 4-209. The fees and procedure match PetData's current pages, so no step depends on the gap.

Policy judgement for the user: 31 County Code quotes (and the adoption record) were read through the Legistar Web API (webapi.legistar.com, no robots.txt; Granicus's published interface to public Legistar items) because albemarle.legistar1.com's robots.txt disallows all crawlers (rechecked 2026-10-11). The verifier judged this acceptable, as in the earlier Albemarle business license verification. If the user disagrees, those quotes should come out.

Not established from any source: whether the Finance & Budget office sells licenses in person, PetData's fax number and mailbox for Albemarle documents, how a service-dog owner claims the exemption, whether a kennel must use a kennel license, how releasing agencies register, the SPCA's reclaim fees and hours, the 2025 shelter agreement, a rabies clinic schedule, and an ordinance setting the $35 returned-payment fee. Each is stated as unknown in the caveats; none makes a step wrong.

Privacy: no staff names or direct lines are recorded. The one mailbox, CAHDEH@vdh.virginia.gov, is listed under 'How to Contact Us' on the Blue Ridge Health District's Environmental Health page for the Charlottesville/Albemarle Health Department office; lexflow's privacy guard (lexflow/privacy.py, whole-token rule) classes its local part as personal-looking because the initialism cannot be derived from the row's label, so renderers will hide it unless the guard is given the office's full name.
